title: Platform 4, 3:12 AM
description: A single fluorescent tube hums above rows of empty benches. The departure board has gone blank for the night, and a paper cup drifts along the tiles in the draft. No one is waiting for anything.

title: Last Announcement
description: Field recording from a deserted railway concourse after midnight: the echo of a recorded voice announcing a train no one will board, the buzz of a vending machine, and footsteps that belong only to the cleaner.

title: Gate 31
description: Oil on canvas. An airport gate in the blue hour before dawn; a lone traveller sleeps curled across three plastic seats while the runway lights blink through a vast black window.

title: Night Bus
description: The driver and I / have stopped pretending / we are going anywhere. / Streetlights pass like slow thoughts. / Every stop is empty, / and every stop we stop anyway.

title: Laundromat, 2 AM
description: A brightly lit laundromat on an otherwise dark street. One dryer turns. A man sits alone scrolling through nothing on his phone, his reflection floating in the glass like a second, even quieter stranger.

title: Night Shift
description: A nurse eats cold noodles in a hospital break room at 4 AM. The corridor outside is silent except for monitors beeping far away. She types a message to someone, deletes it, and sends nothing.

title: The Unoccupied Chair
description: A bronze chair bolted to the middle of an empty city square, lit by a single streetlamp. Visitors say that at night it looks less like furniture and more like someone who has been waiting too long.

title: Ghost Signal
description: Radio static at the edge of the dial, / a voice that almost says my name. / The whole city is asleep / and I am the last lit window, / tuning in to nobody.

title: Polaroid, August 1998
description: A faded instant photo of two kids on bicycles at the end of a dusty lane, their shadows long in the late-summer sun. The colours have drifted toward orange, as if the afternoon itself is slowly leaving.

title: Ice-Cream Van, Far Away
description: The tinny melody of an ice-cream van heard from several streets away on a warm evening, mixed with distant children shouting and a screen door slamming. It fades out before you can run to catch it.

title: Grandmother's Kitchen
description: Cardamom and burnt milk, / the radio playing songs older than my mother, / my feet not yet reaching the floor. / I did not know then / that a kitchen could be a whole country / you are exiled from by growing up.

title: Last Day of the Holidays
description: Watercolour of a beach at dusk after the tourists have gone: a forgotten plastic bucket, a half-collapsed sandcastle, and the sea quietly erasing the footprints of a summer that is already over.

title: The Old Cartoon
description: A grown man, alone in his apartment, finds a VHS tape of the cartoon he watched every Saturday morning. He laughs at the first scene and then, unexpectedly, has to pause it.

title: Outgrown
description: A child's school uniform cast in white plaster, hung on a hook far too low for any adult. Visitors have to crouch down to read the name tag stitched inside the collar.

title: Rooftop Kites
description: Black-and-white photograph of boys flying paper kites from flat rooftops in an old neighbourhood that has since been demolished. The sky is full of them; the buildings no longer exist.

title: Cassette
description: I rewound it with a pencil / so many times the song went thin. / Now it plays in my head / at the wrong speed, / and still I know every crackle.

title: The Eid Express
description: A crowded night train packed with families travelling home for the holidays. Children run between the seats, strangers share sweets and tea, and the whole carriage bursts into laughter when a baby sneezes.

title: Night Market
description: A narrow street at midnight glowing with paper lanterns and food stalls. Steam rises from grills, music spills from a speaker, and a crowd of friends clinks glasses under a string of coloured bulbs.

title: Wedding Drums
description: A recording from a courtyard wedding: dhol drums, clapping, ululation, and a crowd breaking into dance. The rhythm keeps accelerating until it dissolves into cheering.

title: Fireworks Over the Harbour
description: Bursts of gold and violet paint thrown across a black sky above crowded docks. Thousands of tiny upturned faces are suggested with single dots of white, every one of them looking up at once.

title: Street Party
description: Somebody brought a trumpet, / somebody brought a pot of rice, / by nine the whole block was dancing / and nobody could remember / whose idea it had been.

title: First Monsoon
description: Children in school uniforms dancing barefoot in the first heavy rain of the season, arms spread wide, mouths open to the sky, splashing through brown puddles while adults laugh from the doorways.

title: Confetti Fountain
description: A kinetic installation that bursts into a cloud of paper confetti whenever visitors clap together. The louder the room, the higher it goes.

title: Goal!
description: A packed neighbourhood cafe erupts as the underdog team scores in the final minute. Strangers hug, chairs fall over, and an old man stands on a table waving a flag.

title: Answering Machine
description: An old answering machine plays a saved message from a father who has since died: an ordinary reminder to buy bread. The tape hiss continues for a long time after his voice ends.

title: The Empty Place Setting
description: A dinner table set for a family of four, painted in muted greys. Three plates are full; the fourth plate, glass and folded napkin are untouched, lit more brightly than anything else in the room.

title: Inventory
description: His coat still on the hook. / His handwriting on the calendar / for a Tuesday he never reached. / I keep finding him in small things, / and every time / I lose him again.

title: Umbrellas
description: A cemetery in heavy rain seen from above: a tight circle of black umbrellas around an open grave, and one small yellow umbrella held by a child standing slightly apart.

title: Cello for an Empty Room
description: A slow solo cello lament recorded in an unfurnished apartment, the notes echoing off bare walls. Halfway through, the player stops, breathes unevenly, and begins again.

title: Ashes at Sea
description: Two adult siblings on a small boat scatter their mother's ashes over grey water. The wind blows some of the ash back onto their coats, and they begin, helplessly, to laugh and cry at the same time.

title: Hollow Figure
description: A life-size human silhouette cut out of a steel sheet, so that the viewer sees the landscape through the space where a person should be. It is named after the sculptor's late brother.

title: The House After
description: We turned off the lights one by one / the night after the funeral, / and the house went dark / the way a face does / when it finally stops pretending.

title: Green Through Ash
description: A single bright green shoot pushing up through black charcoal in a forest burned the previous summer. Behind it, blurred, more green dots are appearing on the scorched ground.

title: Morning After
description: The storm took the fence / and half the roof, / but the kettle still works, / and the neighbour is already at the door / with a ladder and a joke.

title: First Light Over the Ward
description: Dawn light spilling through a hospital window onto a patient sitting up in bed for the first time in weeks, reaching for a cup of tea with both hands.

title: Thaw
description: Recording of a frozen river in early spring: cracks, drips, and then the first trickle of running water under the ice, joined by a single bird testing its voice.

title: Learning to Walk Again
description: A woman with a new prosthetic leg takes her first unassisted steps across a physiotherapy room while her daughter films on a phone, both of them trying not to cry.

title: Kintsugi Bowl
description: A shattered clay bowl reassembled with seams of gold lacquer, displayed so that the repaired cracks catch the light. The label reads: more beautiful for having broken.

title: Rebuilding
description: Volunteers passing bricks hand to hand along a line to rebuild a school after an earthquake. Everyone is covered in dust; several of them are smiling.

title: Seed Packet
description: Plant them anyway, / she said, in the winter of the diagnosis, / and in April / the whole balcony was tomatoes.

title: Rush Hour, Line 2
description: An underground train at peak hour: screeching brakes, overlapping announcements, a door alarm beeping, hundreds of shuffling feet, and someone shouting to be let off before the doors close.

title: Deadline
description: Expressionist canvas of an office worker's face split into a dozen overlapping screens, each one showing a different notification, the colours clashing in acid green and red.

title: Crossing
description: Long-exposure photograph of a crowded intersection in which every pedestrian is a blur except one man standing perfectly still in the centre with his hands over his ears.

title: Inbox
description: Forty-one unread, / the pulse in my wrist / keeping time with the typing, / and somewhere under all of it / a version of me / that used to sleep.

title: Traffic Jam
description: Hours into a gridlocked highway, horns blaring. A driver's phone battery dies, the air conditioning fails, and she starts laughing in a way that sounds close to panic.

title: Noise Tower
description: A tower of hundreds of stacked, mismatched speakers, each playing a different city sound (sirens, drilling, alarms, ringtones) so that standing inside it feels physically overwhelming.

title: Open-Plan Office
description: An open-plan office at five on a Friday: phones ringing, keyboards clattering, a printer jamming, and fragments of a dozen tense conversations about missed targets.

title: Neon Insomnia
description: An apartment window at 3 AM in a city that never sleeps: a tired face lit blue by a laptop, while outside the billboards flash advertisements to empty streets.

title: Mist on the Lake
description: Early morning mist lying on a perfectly still lake, a single wooden rowing boat tied to a jetty, and pine trees fading into the white. Nothing moves.

title: Forest Dawn Chorus
description: Forty minutes of birdsong recorded in a beech forest at sunrise, with a stream running softly in the background and the occasional rustle of leaves.

title: Tea Fields
description: Soft green terraces of tea bushes rolling down a hillside under a pale early sky, a few pickers with baskets moving slowly between the rows.

title: Stillness
description: The heron does not hurry. / The water does not ask / what time it is. / For one long breath / neither do I.

title: Rain on a Tin Roof
description: Gentle, steady rain on the corrugated tin roof of a mountain hut, thunder rolling somewhere far away, and a kettle beginning to whistle.

title: Moss Garden
description: A shallow basin of living moss and smooth river stones in a quiet courtyard, raked sand around it, and a bamboo spout that tips water every few minutes.

title: Canoe at Sunrise
description: A slow, wordless shot of a canoe gliding across a glassy river as the sun rises; the only sounds are the paddle dipping and a kingfisher calling from the reeds.

title: Desert Dawn
description: Rippled sand dunes turning from violet to gold in the first light, a single line of camel tracks leading toward the horizon under an enormous, silent sky.

title: Under One Umbrella
description: The forecast said nothing about you. / We shared the umbrella / and both got wet anyway, / and neither of us / walked any faster.

title: Two Cups
description: Two coffee cups on a cafe table beside a rain-streaked window, one with a lipstick mark, their handles turned toward each other as if the cups are also holding hands.

title: Old Couple Dancing
description: An elderly couple slow-dancing in their small kitchen to a song on the radio, her head on his shoulder, his slippers slightly out of step.

title: Voice Note
description: A shy, rambling voice message recorded late at night: someone trying to say that they are falling for you, restarting the sentence three times and laughing nervously.

title: Airport Reunion
description: After two years apart, a couple spots each other across the arrivals hall; she drops her bag and runs, and they collide in a hug that nearly knocks over a luggage trolley.

title: Love Locks
description: A bridge railing rebuilt inside the gallery, heavy with thousands of padlocks engraved with initials and dates, some of them rusted almost shut.

title: Six Time Zones
description: You are six time zones away, / so I wake at your midnight / just to be awake / in the same darkness / as you.

title: Letters
description: A bundle of handwritten letters tied with faded ribbon on a windowsill, the top envelope addressed in careful, hopeful handwriting and stamped return to sender.

title: Milky Way Over the Desert
description: The band of the Milky Way arching over a dark desert, with a single tiny human figure holding a headlamp on a rock at the bottom of the frame, dwarfed by billions of stars.

title: Plasma Waves
description: Eerie whistles and hums converted from electromagnetic data recorded by a probe drifting beyond the edge of the solar system.

title: Speck
description: From far enough away / every war we ever fought / fits on a speck of dust / hanging in a sunbeam. / I find this / oddly comforting.

title: Nebula Study
description: Swirling clouds of magenta and teal dust in which new stars are faintly igniting, painted on a canvas nine metres wide so that visitors must step back to take it all in.

title: Earthrise
description: An astronaut looks through a small window as the Earth rises over the grey lunar horizon, and she realises that everyone she has ever known is on that small blue marble.

title: Scale Model
description: A room-sized installation in which the Sun is a beach ball at one end of the gallery and the Earth a peppercorn forty metres away; the nearest star would be in another country.

title: Deep Field
description: A telescope image of a patch of sky no bigger than a grain of sand held at arm's length, containing thousands of galaxies, each holding billions of stars.

title: Stargazing Lesson
description: My father pointed at a star / and said its light was older than our family name. / I was nine. / I have been small / ever since, and glad of it.

title: Barricade
description: Protesters in thick smoke behind a burning barricade at night, one woman clinging to a lamppost with a megaphone, her mouth open mid-shout.

title: Enough
description: They told us to be patient / for forty years. / We were patient. / Now we are something else.

title: The Clenched Fist
description: A huge red fist bursting through a cracked concrete wall, painted in thick, violent strokes across the side of a factory.

title: March
description: Thousands of voices chanting in unison, drums and whistles, and the rising roar of a crowd refusing to disperse as police sirens approach.

title: Eviction
description: A family's furniture is thrown onto the pavement in the rain while the landlord watches from his car; the teenage son stares at him with a fury that needs no words.

title: Broken Scales
description: A bronze scale of justice with one pan melted and bent, weighed down by a pile of cheap coins, left on the steps of a courthouse without permission.

title: Basement Show
description: A sweaty basement concert: the singer screams into the microphone while fans slam into each other in the mosh pit under a single red bulb.

title: Factory Whistle
description: Twelve hours for bread, / and the owner's dog / eats better than my children. / Do not tell me / to lower my voice.

title: Abandoned Station
description: An abandoned railway station swallowed by jungle: vines through the ticket window, a tree growing up through the platform, and sunlight falling on a rusted clock stopped at 3:15.

title: Still Life with Rotting Fruit
description: A lavish bowl of fruit painted in the old Dutch style, but on closer inspection the peaches are bruising, a fly rests on the grapes, and the candle has almost burned out.

title: Rust Horse
description: A life-size horse welded from car parts and left outdoors for twenty years; it is slowly rusting away, and the museum has decided to let it.

title: Mirror
description: The face in the mirror / has started to resemble my father's, / which is strange, / because I was sure / I was the one who stayed young.

title: Clock Shop
description: Dozens of antique clocks ticking slightly out of sync in a small shop, while a grandfather clock slowly chimes the hour over all the rest.

title: Time-Lapse House
description: A time-lapse of one house over fifty years: the children grow up and leave, the paint peels, the garden goes wild, and finally a bulldozer arrives.

title: Sandcastle Tide
description: A detailed sandcastle photographed once a minute as the tide comes in; the final frame shows only smooth, wet sand.

title: Ruins at Dusk
description: Crumbling columns of an ancient temple silhouetted against a red sky, goats grazing where emperors once held court.

title: The Long Way Home
description: After ten years working abroad, a man steps off a dusty bus in his village; his mother, now white-haired, recognises his walk before she can see his face.

title: Arrivals, Central Station
description: A crowded station platform at dawn; a young soldier in uniform lifts his little sister off the ground as their parents rush toward them.

title: Doorframe
description: The pencil marks are still there, / each birthday a little higher, / my name in my mother's handwriting. / I stand against them now / and the house says: you're back.

title: Mother Tongue
description: An airport arrivals hall where, after hours of foreign announcements, a returning traveller suddenly hears a group of old men arguing cheerfully in her native dialect.

title: Lamp in the Window
description: A small farmhouse at night in deep snow, with a single warm lamp left burning in the window for someone who is still on the road.

title: Keys
description: A wall of hundreds of old house keys donated by refugees who still carry the keys to homes they were forced to leave, each tagged with the name of a village.

title: Sunday Lunch
description: Three generations crowded around a table too small for them, passing dishes over each other's heads, everybody talking at once.

title: Old Friends
description: Two men who were inseparable as boys meet again after thirty years at a roadside tea stall and, within minutes, are teasing each other exactly as they used to.

title: Footsteps
description: A woman walks home alone down an empty street at night and slowly realises that the footsteps behind her stop whenever she stops.

title: Deep Sea Hydrophone
description: Low groans and unexplained clicks captured by a hydrophone in a pitch-black ocean trench, kilometres below where any sunlight reaches.

title: The Visitor
description: A child's bedroom at night painted in dark blues; the wardrobe door is open a crack, and something inside it seems to be looking back.

title: Basement
description: Count the stairs going down. / Now count them coming up. / Tell me why / there is one more.

title: Fog Forest
description: A dense pine forest swallowed by fog at dusk, the trunks fading to grey, and a figure, or perhaps a tree stump, standing far off between them.

title: Watchers
description: Rows of faceless porcelain dolls arranged along a dim corridor, each head turned slightly toward the entrance so that visitors feel observed as they walk past.

title: Static Call
description: A phone call recorded at 3 AM in which there is only breathing and static for two minutes before the line suddenly goes dead.

title: Wildfire Road
description: A family's car speeds down a road with walls of fire on both sides, the sky orange and black, and embers hitting the windscreen like rain.

title: The Very Serious Duck
description: A three-metre rubber duck wearing a judge's wig and reading glasses, installed without explanation in the lobby of a law school.

title: Cats Holding a Board Meeting
description: A formal oil portrait of seven cats in business suits around a boardroom table, one of them pushing a glass of water off the edge while making eye contact with the viewer.

title: Complaint from a Sock
description: I was one of a pair. / Then came the washing machine. / I have questions, / and I have lawyers.

title: Goat Choir
description: A field recording of a herd of goats bleating in something almost like harmony, remixed with a church organ so that it sounds like a very confused choir.

title: The Wrong Wedding
description: A best man delivers a heartfelt, tearful speech, then slowly realises he is at the wrong couple's wedding; the guests are too moved to stop him.

title: Dog in Sunglasses
description: A pug in tiny sunglasses riding in a bicycle basket, ears flapping, looking far cooler than the man pedalling.

title: Gravity Is Optional
description: Furniture glued upside down to the gallery ceiling (a dining table, chairs, a cat bed) with a dinner party apparently in full swing.

title: Instructions for the Toaster
description: Do not trust it. / It knows what you did / to the waffle iron.

title: Departure
description: A ship's deck at dawn as it pulls away from the harbour, a young woman at the railing with a single suitcase, watching her hometown shrink behind her.

title: Open Road
description: Wind roaring through the open windows of a car on a coastal highway, a song on the radio half drowned out, gulls and the sea somewhere below.

title: Map
description: Every place I have not been / is folded in my pocket, / soft at the creases / from being opened / so many times.

title: Caravan at Night
description: A line of camels crossing moonlit dunes toward a distant oasis, lanterns swinging, one traveller singing to keep the others awake.

title: Sleeper Compartment
description: Two strangers share a sleeper compartment on an overnight train across the steppe, trading life stories until dawn as the endless grassland rolls past the window.

title: Suitcase Tower
description: Dozens of battered suitcases stacked into a leaning tower, each one covered in faded stickers from cities around the world.

title: Summit
description: A hiker on a mountain peak at sunrise with both arms raised, a sea of clouds stretching to the horizon below.

title: Harbour at Dusk
description: Ropes creaking, halyards clinking against masts, waves slapping the hulls of moored boats, and a foghorn sounding once from somewhere out at sea.

title: Blackout
description: A neighbourhood during a city-wide power cut: every house is dark, but families have carried candles and guitars up to the rooftops and are calling jokes to each other across the street.

title: Glow Stars
description: Plastic glow-in-the-dark stars stuck to the ceiling of a childhood bedroom, half of them fallen off, photographed on the day the family house was sold.

title: Funeral Bell
description: A single church bell tolling slowly over a village, muffled sobbing from the mourners, and gravel crunching under the slow steps of the pallbearers.

title: Downpour Tango
description: Caught without umbrellas, two strangers at a bus stop give up on staying dry and begin an improvised tango in the downpour while passengers cheer from the bus windows.

title: Grey Weeks
description: A figure lying on a sofa in a room where everything has turned grey (the walls, the unopened post, the untouched meals) while through the window the street outside is still in full colour.
